data.claim: With needs_apply=phase a task under a phase with unfinished needs is ready; with tasks or the task inherit flag it is blocked naming the phase edge
data.falsifier: The default-phase test still sees the task blocked, or an opted-in task ready
data.mechanism: inherited_deps is the single path all readiness and wave views use; gating the ancestor pairs by graph_needs.binds_descendant changes all of them together
data.probe: uv run pytest tests/test_phase_needs_scope.py with binds_descendant forced to return True
data.question: Do phase needs bind tasks only when opted in, via one fold-level rule?

chunk_findings.detail: The guard only rejects `inherit` on phases (`it.kind == "phase"`), not on other non-task kinds. Given `update(repo, "BUG-1", ItemEdit(inherit=True))` (or a generic `bug update BUG-1 --set inherit=true` path), `_scope_refusal` returns `None` because the item kind is not `"phase"`, then `_fields` sets `fields["inherit"] = True` and the update persists a task-only opt-in on a bug. The accepted semantics say `inherit` is a task's flag, so non-task, non-phase items should be refused; otherwise unrelated records can carry inheritance state that doctor/why-blocked or later need-binding code may misinterpret.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items/_edit.py:_scope_refusal

chunk_findings.detail: `phase_lift` treats the lift as successful even when the required decision cannot be created. It calls `decision_add(...)`, then does `did = str(dec.data.get("id", "")) if dec.ok else ""` and unconditionally executes `log.append(KIND, ...)` and returns `O.ok(...)`. If `decision_add` returns a failed outcome (for example, a draft validation/dedupe failure), the function still records a `phase.need_lifted` event and reports success with `decision=""`. That violates the stated audited-lift semantics: the lift becomes active with no recorded decision id.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/phases.py:phase_lift

chunk_findings.detail: The new `[phases]` knob documents the default `phase` scope as making tasks *not* inherit a phase's needs unless they opt in (`inherit` or `needs_apply=tasks`). That directly contradicts the listed advisory rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave], whose CHECK states that a task inherits the needs of its phase. Under the new default (`phases.needs_apply_default = "phase"`), a task under a phase whose phase-level need is still open can be claimable, whereas the advisory rule requires the task to be treated as blocked by the phase need.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/phases.py:20

chunk_findings.detail: The new `phase lift` command declares its payload as `("id", "need", "why", "undo", "decision")`, but its parameters and handler use `reason`: `Param("reason", ...)` and `a.get("reason", "")`. If `payload` is the agent/tool-facing payload key list, a call using the documented `reason` field is not accepted, while a call using the only payload reason field `why` reaches the lambda but is ignored, so the API sees an empty reason even though the command description says `--reason` is required. The mismatch is reinforced by `tool_order=("id", "need", "reason", "undo")` naming `reason` while `payload` omits it and includes `why`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/phase_complete.py:LIFT

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds `inherit` as a task field in `task.updated`, and the intent/API/record changes treat task opt-in inheritance as a persisted task flag. However, no corresponding `task.added` event kind was updated in this change: `items.toml` only adds `phase.need_lifted`, `links.toml` only changes `phase.added`, and `model.toml` only changes `phase.updated`/`task.updated`. Given `ddflow task add T --phase P --inherit`, the add path emits a `task.added` payload containing `inherit=true`, but the add event schema does not declare that field. Depending on event validation strictness, the add is rejected or the field is dropped during replay/upgrade, so after replay the task is no longer opted in and becomes claimable under a `needs_apply=phase` phase, violating the requirement that the opt-in survive replay.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/events/model.toml:26 (`task.updated` / missing `task.added` schema)

chunk_findings.detail: The `globs` help still states: “the phase's dependencies are INHERITED by every task in it.” That is now false under the accepted default `needs_apply=phase`: a task under a phase whose need is open is claimable by default and inherits only if the task opts in or the phase uses `needs_apply=tasks`. For example, after `ddflow phase add P --needs-apply phase` (or with the new default), an agent reading `phase add --help`/`phase update --help` is told tasks inherit the phase need, then adds `ddflow task add T --phase P` expecting it to be blocked, but the task is claimable. The help directly contradicts the newly added `needs_apply` help and the new semantics.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/queue.py (`globs` Param help)

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s stated docs deliverable is “README row, help topic, knob register entry,” but the 30-file manifest contains help and knob-register templates and no README/docs-table file. Given a user looking for the new `[phases].needs_apply_default` / `phase --needs-apply` row in the README, the row is absent, so the documented acceptance docs are incomplete.
chunk_findings.title: manifest / README.md

chunk_findings.detail: The new help text makes task inheritance opt-in (`--needs-apply tasks` or task `inherit=true`, default `phase`), directly contradicting the recorded advisory rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave], which says a task inherits the needs of its phase. Concretely, with phase `P2` needing `P1` and task `T` under `P2`, the new default makes `T` claimable while `P1` is open, whereas the rule says the phase needs govern the task. The change does not amend or replace that guidance.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/workflow.md:10-14

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "P2" in b["detail"]` does not actually verify that the blocked view names the phase inheritance edge. If `next` returns a detail string such as `"P2.T1 is blocked by P1"`, the test still passes because `"P2"` is a substring of the task ID `"P2.T1"`, even though the phase `P2` edge was not named. This can hide a real defect where tasks are blocked but the required inheritance path is omitted from the blocked/why-blocked output.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_phase_needs_scope.py:test_opt_in_phase_tasks_inherit

chunk_findings.detail: The update path copies `edit.needs_apply` into the record fields without checking it against `GN.NEEDS_APPLY`, unlike `phase_add` in `ddflow/api/items/_add.py`, which validates the value before writing it. Given `update(repo, "phase-1", ItemEdit(needs_apply="taks"))` (or the equivalent `--set needs_apply=taks`), `_fields` stores `needs_apply="taks"` and the update can succeed. A later scope check that compares the field to `"tasks"` (as the effective-edge logic implied by `binds_descendant` would) then treats the phase as `phase` scope, so tasks under it remain claimable when the user intended `tasks` scope; if a projection expects only `phase|tasks`, replay can also break.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items/_edit.py:_fields

chunk_findings.detail: `_scope_refusal` is documented as rejecting a task-only `inherit` flag on anything that is not a task, but it only rejects `inherit` when `it.kind == "phase"`. Given `update(repo, "bug-1", ItemEdit(inherit=True))`, the guard falls through because a bug is not a phase, then `_fields` writes `fields["inherit"] = True`. Thus a bug or lesson can receive the task opt-in flag, contrary to the stated flag semantics and potentially visible to any projection that reads `inherit` without filtering by item kind.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items/_edit.py:_scope_refusal

chunk_findings.detail: `phase_lift` requires a recorded decision, but it still records the lift and returns success when `decision_add` fails. After `dec = decision_add(...)`, line 73 sets `did` to `""` when `dec.ok` is false, then line 74 unconditionally appends the `phase.need_lifted` event and line 75 returns `O.ok`. Thus, for any non-ok decision outcome (for example a duplicate or invalid decision draft), the edge is lifted without the required decision/audit trail, contrary to the function contract and the accepted governance decision.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/phases.py:74

chunk_findings.detail: The recorded rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave] says that a task inherits the needs of its phase. This knob makes the default binding `phase`, so a task placed under a phase with an open need and no explicit need is not blocked by that need. For example, with `phases.needs_apply_default = "phase"` (the default), phase `p` has need `docs` open and task `t` is in `p`; `t` is claimable, while the rule expects `t` to inherit `docs` and be blocked. The rule is advisory, so this is a low-severity violation/risk.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/phases.py:needs_apply_default [r-task-phase-needs-wave]

chunk_findings.detail: The function is documented as returning phases “whose tasks inherit the phase's needs only because no scope was ever chosen” and whose behaviour a migration to `phase` would change, but the predicate only checks `st.descendants(p.id)`; it never inspects the descendants' `inherit` flag. Given a legacy phase `p` with `needs_apply=""`, `needs=["a"]`, and a single child task `t` with `inherit=True`, `legacy_inheriting_phases` returns `p` and `doctor_notes` emits `--needs-apply phase` “would stop that”. However, after migrating `p` to `needs_apply="phase"`, `binds_descendant(p, t)` still returns true because `t.inherit` is true, so the migration changes no behaviour. The doctor therefore lists a phase as needing migration when its only descendants have already opted in.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/graph_needs.py:legacy_inheriting_phases

chunk_findings.detail: The `LIFT` command declares its payload as `("id", "need", "why", "undo", "decision")`, but its `call` lambda reads `a.get("reason", "")` and the declared `Param` is named `reason`. If the command is invoked through the declared tool payload (e.g. `ddflow_phase_lift` with `{"id": "p", "need": "n", "why": "..."}`), the reason is passed under `why`, `a.get("reason")` is empty, and `_api().phase_lift(..., reason="")` is called even though the command says the reason is required and audited. Conversely, a caller that supplies `reason` is not using the declared payload field. This silently drops the required lift reason (or makes the tool call fail if `phase_lift` enforces it).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/phase_complete.py:LIFT payload

chunk_findings.detail: The `globs` help still states that “the phase's dependencies are INHERITED by every task in it,” which contradicts the newly introduced `needs_apply` semantics and the accepted default that tasks do not inherit phase needs unless opted in. Given an agent running `ddflow phase add --help` or consulting this help, it may omit task needs or place a task under a `needs_apply=phase` phase expecting automatic inheritance, while the actual behavior makes the task claimable prematurely.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/queue.py (globs Param)

chunk_findings.detail: The new help text and behavior make phase-need inheritance opt-in for tasks, but this contradicts the recorded advisory rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave], whose CHECK says “a task inherits the needs of its phase.” For example, after `ddflow phase add P --needs P1` with the new default `phase`, a task `T` in `P` is claimable while `P1` is open; under [r-task-phase-needs-wave] it should inherit `P1` and be blocked. The change either needs to update/supersede that rule or otherwise align the docs/behavior with it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/workflow.md

fields.body:
RULE: every task names the phase whose progress it counts towards, states its dependencies in needs, and carries a wave:N tag (ddflow waves --stamp derives it). A task with no prerequisite carries the tag no-deps, so that none is a decision and not an omission. Work that blocks a phase belongs in that phase; a catch-all such as bugs-2 is only for work no phase serves. This covers tasks ddflow files itself, including bug fix tasks.
CHECK: a phase's needs bind the phase itself (D-phase-needs-scope-accepted-2026-11-11): its tasks inherit them only when the phase has needs_apply = tasks, the task has inherit = true, or the phase predates the flag (doctor lists those). So state a task's own prerequisites in its needs, and read the phase's needs_apply before relying on inheritance. ddflow waves --check reports stale stamps.
VERIFY: which phase counts this task, what must land first (in its own needs), and is its wave current?
fields.title: Every task has a phase, stated dependencies and a wave tag

For a non-task, non-phase item such as a bug, `update(repo, "BUG-1", ItemEdit(inherit=True))` reaches `_scope_refusal` with `edit.needs_apply is None` and `it.kind != "phase"`, so the `elif edit.inherit is not None and it.kind == "phase"` branch is false and the function returns `None`. The accepted semantics say `inherit` is a task-only opt-in flag, so a bug-level `inherit=True` should be refused; as written, the wrong-kind guard is incomplete for any kind other than phase/task.

chunk_findings.detail: The changed predicate for unmigrated phases now omits an existing phase whose current tasks all have `inherit` truthy. Given phase `P` with no explicit `needs_apply`, a phase-level need, and only one task `P.T` with `inherit=True`, the expression `any(not st.items[t].inherit for t in st.descendants(p.id))` is false, so `P` is not listed by the doctor/migration path. The accepted decision requires existing phases to keep their inherited behavior until migrated and to be listed for the one-line migration; `P` is still unmigrated, and a future task added to `P` would depend on that legacy unset state, but the doctor no longer surfaces it.
